choices.misconception: I thought that adding and taking away numbers that are so close together cancels out to nothing.
I worked out $1000 - 999 = 1$ and thought the whole thing would come to that same 1.
I made pairs that each give 1, but only counted two of the three pairs.
I thought each pair like $1000 - 999$ makes 2, because the numbers go down by 2 each time.

hints: Look at the numbers two at a time.
Group the calculation into pairs: a number minus the number just below it. Each pair is easy to work out.

solutions.reliable: Group into pairs: $(1000 - 999) + (998 - 997) + (996 - 995) = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3$. The transferable idea: regroup a long calculation into pairs that are easy to work out.

whyOnTest: Clever regrouping turns a scary calculation with big numbers into three easy pairs.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
